newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL - EWING ADMITS TO SCOREBOARD WATCHING.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL - EWING ADMITS TO SCOREBOARD WATCHING.

text.p: Call it basketball's first sign of spring -- and the playoffs.
New York Knicks centre Patrick Ewing admitted to a little baseball-style scoreboard watching in Tuesday's 93-86 win over the Milwaukee Bucks.

Ewing, who earlier had bruised his knee, left the game with a little over six minutes to go, his team holding a seemingly comfortable 16-point lead and a chance to vault past the Miami Heat into first place in the Atlantic Division.

Explaining the importance of the division lead requires two words: Michael Jordan. After the playoffs start in late April, the division winner will avoid Jordan's league-leading, defending-champion Chicago Bulls until the Eastern Conference finals.

The game apparently in hand, Ewing left the bench for the clubhouse, where he watched with mounting concern as the television showed the Bucks running off the next 15 points to cut the New York lead to a single point.
In addition, his scoreboard-watching brought him the unsettling news that Miami, leading the Knicks by a half game in the division, had upset the Pistons in Detroit.
Ewing decided to go back into the game, hurting knee and all. "They made a run at us," said Ewing. "I saw that Miami had won, also. This was a game that we need, so I got back out there."
Knicks coach Jeff Van Gundy had been told by trainer Mike Saunders not to expect Ewing back. "Mike told me he was out for the night," said Van Gundy.
The coach conferred with his star asset before sending him into the game. "I asked him if he was ready to play," said Van Gundy.
Ewing remembered it a little differently. "If it hurts too bad, sit your butt down," Ewing quoted his coach as saying.
As Ewing waited to go in, forward Larry Johnson produced the play of the game, a power basket down low plus a free throw to give New York an 88-84 lead.

Then Ewing went in, and helped shore up the defence while scoring a point on a free throw as the Knicks averted an embarrassing loss. He wound up sharing the team high in scoring with Johnson: 17 points.
He said if he had seen Johnson's shot from the locker room, he might well not have come back out.

Van Gundy conceded that expectations had been that Miami, without injured centre Alonzo Mourning, would fall in Detroit and the Knicks would climb into first place, given Milwaukee's relatively weak record. But he said he would have bucked the odds and picked Miami over Detroit if he were betting.
"It never works out like you think in the NBA," said Van Gundy. "You never look past anybody."
Ewing bruised his knee early in the third quarter in a collision with Bucks point guard Sherman Douglas. "He tried to trap me," said Ewing. "We banged knees."
He said he hoped to be able to play in games Wednesday in Toronto and Friday in Boston against two of the NBA's worst teams, ahead of Sunday's showdown in New York with the Bulls.
"It's sore. I'm sure it'll be a little sore tonight," Ewing said of the knee.
